title: STG-12 — Day 2 Counter Interaction (Boarding Denial & Pattern Confirmation)
subtitle: Overnight ban persists; LATAM Official says '¡Cállate!'; shifting narratives challenged; independent witness evidence; 85% flight monopoly confirmed
location: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport, Santiago, Chile — LATAM Counter
classification: Attorney Work Product — Privileged and Confidential

participants.role: LATAM Supervisor — shift change, initially confused, denies boarding
LATAM Official — dismissive, says '¡Cállate!', refers to constancia
Unidentified LATAM or airport staff — says 'Thank you' at end

violations_cited: LPDC Art. 23 bis — failure to provide lawful written reasons
CPCL Art. 197 — falsification of private document (unsigned carta)
CPCL Art. 211 (CHIPENCOD) — calumnia (false accusation of aggression)
CACH Art. 133 — denied‑boarding compensation not offered
CACH Art. 131 — no rights information provided
LPDC Art. 3(b) — right to truthful information violated
Systemic institutional practice — daily false detentions confirmed by Carabineros (cross‑reference)
Abuso de autoridad — forcible removal without valid cause
Lifetime travel ban without due process (85% market share)

key_evidentiary_findings.finding: Boarding ban persists overnight across shift change — 'No puede embarcar.' The 'disruptivo' label (F-019) remains active, confirming system‑wide implementation of the travel ban.
Supervisor confuses timeline — asks '¿qué hizo anoche?' Leandro corrects that the incident occurred at 1 PM, not last night. Indicates poor information transfer between shifts.
Core claim restated consistently: 'La PDI vio la cámara y comprobó que no pasó nada.' Leandro offers to verify with PDI. Account matches all prior recordings.
LATAM Official (SPEAKER_03) says '¡Cállate!' — an overtly dismissive, silencing command. Reinforces power asymmetry and contrasts with passenger's documented calm bearing.
Carabineros constancia acknowledged by LATAM staff: 'Esto es una declaración que tú hiciste en cara de dinero.' Indicates the constancia has been shown to them.

Leandro states intent to file individual complaints against the accuser and pilot: 'voy a hacer una denuncia contra las dos personas también.' Moves from institutional complaint to personal accountability.

Shifting‑narratives pattern restated with precision: aggression → camera disproved → boarding pass. '¿Por qué cambiaron de narrativa? ¿Porque una no funcionó?' Consistent across 20+ hours and 7+ interlocutors.
Independent passenger witness: a lady seated next to him 'también no vio nada.' Confirms no aggression occurred. Other passengers questioned the situation collectively.

Leandro possesses audio recordings of LATAM security and DGAC discussing camera evidence. States 'tengo varias grabaciones... no de vídeo, de audio.' Corroborates the existence of the case file recordings.
Lifetime ban scope confirmed: '85 % de los vuelos para donde voy, a la TAM.' Combined with LATAM's monopoly, this constitutes a de facto regional travel prohibition.
Dolo evidence: Leandro asserts LATAM acted 'de propósito, sabiendo que estaban incorrectos' and 'sabiendo que estaban mentindo.' Directly asserts intentionality and knowledge of falsity.
Stigmatisation: Leandro says 'me miran como lo malo.' The 'disruptivo' label primes all interactions with a presumption of passenger wrongdoing, causing psychological harm.
